Since last summer, measures restricting immigration have been raining down in Quebec, as elsewhere in Canada. As an immigrant myself – I arrived a little over two years ago – I broke into a cold sweat with every new announcement. And I’m one of the privileged ones – the “luxury” immigrants, as I call us – who chose to live somewhere else out of desire rather than necessity.
Dans mon quotidien, je croise beaucoup d: In my daily life, I meet many people who came here for different reasons: some fleeing economic hardship, others insecurity, war or even domestic violence. After each new government announcement restricting immigration, many of them had a lot of questions for me.
La confusion et l’inquiétude règnent, co: Confusion and worry are everywhere, as François Loza-Rodriguez confirmed to me when I met him at the offices of the Table de Concertation des organismes au service des personnes réfugiées et immigrantes, where he is the analysis and advocacy coordinator.
J’ai donc décidé d’écrire un article qui: So I decided to write an article that would help make sense of the immigration programs undergoing changes in 2025. For each one, I explain the consequences of the measures, the key dates, the exceptions and more.
<strong>Depuis quelques mois, les annonc: For the past few months, announcements of measures restricting immigration have followed one another, at both the provincial and federal levels. Temporary or permanent worker programs, post-graduation work permits, refugee programs – all have been reshaped with different criteria. It’s hard to find your way when you’re an immigrant. La Converse breaks it down for you.
Depuis plusieurs mois, les politiques d’: For several months now, Quebec’s and Canada’s immigration policies and work programs have undergone a series of <l1>major changes</l1>, making this administrative maze increasingly complex to navigate. Between salary criteria, residency requirements and differences depending on the pathway, some people feel completely lost in a system that is getting harder and harder to understand.
Cette complexité alimente une incertitud: This complexity is fuelling growing uncertainty and a diffuse fear: that of seeing the dream of settling in Canada turn into a real administrative nightmare, with the dread of being sent back to one’s country for failing to meet criteria that are hard to master and change regularly.
À Montréal, dans les bureaux de la <l1>T: In Montréal, at the offices of the <l1>Table de concertation des organismes au service des personnes réfugiées et immigrantes (TCRI)</l1>, a team specializing in immigration issues is working hard to support the 150 member organizations in its network across Quebec and to try to influence the government through its advocacy. On the desks, files are piling up.
« Les mesures prises par les gouvernemen: “The measures taken by governments involve a lot of very technical changes,” says François Loza-Rodriguez, analysis and advocacy coordinator at the TCRI. “It’s already complicated for us to understand all these changes, so imagine for an immigrant who has to go through a whole complex administrative process and who hears news, sometimes contradictory, every week...” he adds.
Lorsque les premières mesures du gouvern: When the Quebec government’s first measures were announced in September 2023, the TCRI put together a webinar, summary documents and all sorts of support for the organizations that work with immigrant populations. “Our members received an enormous number of calls and visits from people who were completely lost and wanted to know whether they were going to be affected by the changes to immigration,” Loza-Rodriguez reports.
Une situation qui persiste aujourd’hui,: That situation persists today, following recent changes to some federal programs. All the more so because the current political context, particularly murky after the announcement of <l1>Justin Trudeau’s resignation</l1> and the possible arrival of a Conservative government, adds to the worry and the questions about the future of immigration policies.
« On est très critiques du gouvernement: “We’re very critical of the government and of all these changes, which suggest a certain amount of improvisation, since some measures have no basis that could justify them. We want people to understand that when there are changes to thresholds or criteria, or anything else, human lives are affected,” insists the analysis and advocacy coordinator. For their part, the Quebec and federal governments cite inflation, the housing crisis and declining labour needs to justify their decisions.
La confusion et la précarité touchent de: Confusion and precarity are affecting many immigration applicants, as well as workers who are already authorized to live here but whose work permit renewal is suddenly called into question. Already vulnerable in the face of the challenges of a new life, they find themselves in an increasingly untenable situation and struggle to sort through the relentless flow of information.
Voilà pourquoi La Converse a décidé de p: That’s why La Converse decided to offer a summary of the main measures.
Le <l1>PTET</l1> permet aux entreprises: The <l1>TFWP</l1> allows businesses to recruit foreign workers to fill positions in a context of labour shortages. These workers receive a so-called “closed” work permit, which ties them to a single employer. If they lose their job, their permit therefore becomes invalid.
Ce programme, souvent critiqué, a été qu: This often-criticized program was described as “a breeding ground for modern forms of slavery” in 2023 by the United Nations Special Rapporteur on contemporary forms of slavery, <l1>Tomoya Obokata</l1>.
Depuis le 3 septembre 2024, les employeu: Since September 3, 2024, employers in the metropolis can no longer submit hiring applications under the TFWP for positions paying less than the gross annual median wage of CAN$57,000. On September 26, similar measures came into effect in provinces where the unemployment rate is above 6%.
La région touchée par le gel d’embauche: The area affected by the hiring freeze, in effect from September 3, 2024, to March 3, 2025, is the census metropolitan area, meaning the following municipalities: Baie‑d’Urfé, Beaconsfield, Côte‑Saint‑Luc, Dollard‑des‑Ormeaux, Dorval, Hampstead, Kirkland, L’Île‑Dorval, Montréal, Montréal‑Est, Montréal‑Ouest, Mont‑Royal, Pointe‑Claire, Sainte‑Anne‑de‑Bellevue, Senneville and Westmount.
Le premier ministre du Québec, François: Quebec Premier François Legault said the decision would apply for a period of six months in Montréal: from September 3, 2024, to March 3, 2025. On the federal side, the end date of the measures is not yet known.
« Les gouvernements du Canada et du Québ: “The governments of Canada and Quebec have agreed to extend the measures available to Quebec employers since 2021 under the TFWP. These measures will remain in place until the annual update, which will take place on February 23, 2025,” reads the official Government of Canada website.
Concrètement, cela signifie que les prof: In practical terms, this means the following occupations are not subject to the restrictions, even in Montréal, until at least February 23, 2025: cashier, school crossing guard, server, kitchen helper, meat cutter, fishmonger, sports or recreation attendant, specialized cleaner, light-duty cleaner, janitor, material handler, delivery driver, taxi driver, agricultural labourer and industrial labourer.
Attention toutefois, car le gouvernement: Be careful, though, because the federal government has lowered the maximum quotas of low-wage temporary foreign workers (TFWs) within businesses in some of these fields. In the construction and health care sectors, the number of TFWs in low-wage positions will be reduced to 20% of a company’s workforce. In other sectors, the current limit of 20% of TFWs in low-wage positions will be lowered to 10%. In practice, this will limit employers’ ability to turn to foreign workers, even if they want to.
Enfin, la durée maximale d’emploi pour d: Finally, the maximum employment duration for low-wage positions will be reduced from two years to one. It will therefore become impossible to obtain permanent residence after two years of employment in Canada if a work permit renewal is refused.
Les options qui s’offrent aux personnes: The options available to immigrants who can no longer renew their closed work permit as a result of the government measures are limited. The first is to find a job in a field covered by an exemption (see above) or to find, in any sector, a job paying $32.96 an hour or more.
La seconde et dernière option est de tro: The second and final option is to find a job, regardless of sector or wage, with a company based outside the Montréal area and outside any region where the unemployment rate is 6% or higher at the time of application. You can keep living in Montréal while working outside the metropolis, for example.
<strong>Le Programme régulier des travai: The Regular Skilled Worker Program (PRTQ), Renamed the Skilled Worker Selection Program (PSTQ) – Provincial
Le 29 novembre 2024, le <l1>Programme de: On November 29, 2024, the <l1>Skilled Worker Selection Program (PSTQ)</l1> replaced the Regular Skilled Worker Program (PRTQ). To submit an application under the PSTQ, you must have received an invitation before that date.
Le PSTQ s’adresse aux personnes qui souh: The PSTQ is for people who want to immigrate to Quebec and obtain permanent residence. Like the PRTQ, this program allows you to declare your interest in immigrating to Quebec as a skilled worker on the Arrima platform, from within Quebec or from abroad. This “declaration of interest” is placed in a pool of applications and ranked according to the number of points your profile earns based on the criteria Quebec is looking for (professional sector, languages, diplomas, family situation, etc.). Only if the person is invited to submit an application for permanent selection can they begin the administrative steps to obtain the permanent resident card, valid for five years.
Jusqu’au 30 juin 2025, le Québec n’enver: Until June 30, 2025, Quebec will no longer send out invitations to submit an application for permanent selection under the PSTQ. This pathway, one of the two main routes to permanent residence, is therefore closed until next summer.
Il n’y a pas vraiment de moyen de contou: There is no real way around this moratorium. Only applications for permanent selection already submitted under the PRTQ are currently being reviewed by Quebec.
Pour ne pas être contraintes de quitter: To avoid being forced to leave the country, immigrants can go through the TFWP to try to keep temporary worker status while waiting for the program to reopen in July 2025.
<strong>Les diplômés exclus du Programme: Graduates Excluded From the Quebec Experience Program (PEQ), Workers Spared – Provincial
En temps normal, le <l1>Programme de l’e: Normally, the <l1>Quebec Experience Program (PEQ)</l1> is very popular with temporary workers and international students who graduate in Quebec. It allows them to obtain a Quebec Selection Certificate to gain access to permanent residence. Workers must have two years of experience in Quebec, while students must have earned an eligible diploma within the last 36 months and have lived in Quebec for at least half of their studies.
Le volet « Diplômés du Québec » du PEQ n: The “Quebec Graduates” stream of the PEQ has not accepted new applications since October 31, 2024, and will not reopen until June 30, 2025.
Pas vraiment… Seules les demandes déposé: Not really… Only applications filed before October 31, 2024, are still being considered by Quebec. It should be noted that requests to add family members, including dependent children and spouses or partners, are not affected by this suspension. It is therefore still possible to submit this type of request under the “Quebec Graduates” stream.
Attention toutefois, car ceux qui sont d: Be careful, though: graduates of a college participating in the public-private agreement have no longer been eligible for the PGWP since May 15, 2024.
<strong>Incompréhension après la fin des: Bewilderment After the End of Private Refugee Sponsorship – Provincial
Le <l1>Programme des personnes réfugiées: The <l1>Refugees Abroad Program</l1> – often called group sponsorship – allows Quebecers to commit to welcoming a refugee and their family who are still abroad.
« C’est l’exemple même d’une décision in: “This is the very example of an incomprehensible decision! In this program, it’s citizens who choose to take on all the costs of bringing a refugee here and welcoming them. On top of that, it only involves a few hundred files a year, so this isn’t what’s going to bring immigration down. On the other hand, it will have terrible consequences for these families, who have dramatic reasons for leaving their country,” explains François Loza-Rodriguez.
Le moratoire est prévu jusqu’au 30 juin: The moratorium is in place until June 30, 2025. Like the previous programs, it will be reassessed during the multi-year immigration planning process, which will take place in the spring.
Ceux qui attendent une décision relative: Those awaiting a decision on their admission as permanent residents are not affected. Sponsorship applications for a dependant of a refugee who is awaiting a decision on admission as a permanent resident are not targeted either.‍
<strong>L’objectif de réunification fami: Family Reunification Target Cut in Half – Provincial
Les citoyens canadiens, les résidents pe: Canadian citizens, permanent residents currently living in Canada and people registered as Indians can sponsor certain family members to allow them to come to Canada with permanent residence.
La personne qui parraine doit également: The sponsor must also be an adult, must not be receiving social assistance other than a disability pension, and must be able to support the people they wish to bring over.
Depuis le 26 juin 2024, le Québec a rédu: Since June 26, 2024, Quebec has reduced the number of accepted <l1>family reunification </l1>applications. The province has set a target of 13,000 people admitted between June 26, 2024, and June 25, 2026. That is half as many as in the previous two years, when 24,416 applications were accepted from 2021 to 2023.
Dans le détail, il est prévu que 10 400: In detail, 10,400 sponsorship applications are expected to be accepted for a spouse, common-law partner or dependent child aged 18 or over. The remaining 2,600 spots are for sponsoring parents, grandparents, orphaned minor siblings, orphaned minor nephews or nieces, and orphaned minor grandchildren.
Une fois que 13 000 personnes auront bén: Once 13,000 people have benefited from family reunification, Quebec will stop receiving applications and will return them to applicants. A first-come, first-served principle therefore applies here, though it should be noted that files that have been waiting for months or even years are currently being processed.
Plusieurs cas ne sont pas concernés par: Several cases are not affected by this lower threshold. These are sponsorship applications for a minor dependent child, a minor child being adopted, an orphaned minor who is the sponsor’s brother, sister, nephew, niece or grandchild, or an adult dependent child who depends on one or both parents because of a physical or mental condition.
Enfin, les demandes soumises pour l’enfa: Finally, applications submitted for the child or spouse of a person already awaiting admission as a permanent resident are also exempt.
<strong>Restriction des permis de travai: Restrictions on Open Work Permits (OWPs) for Family Members of Temporary Residents – Federal
Ce programme permet aux conjoints des tr: This program allows the spouses of temporary foreign workers or international students to obtain an open work permit. This precious key gives them the ability to work for any Canadian employer.
Il y a quelques jours, le gouvernement f: A few days ago, the federal government announced yet another measure. Starting January 21, 2025, only the spouses or common-law partners of certain international students and foreign workers will be able to benefit from an OWP.
Les étudiants qui souhaitent venir avec: Students who want to bring their better half must be enrolled in a master’s program of at least 16 months, a doctoral program or one of the eligible <l1>professional programs</l1>.
Quant aux travailleurs, ils devront doré: As for workers, they will now have to hold a job in TEER category 0 or 1 of the <l1>National Occupational Classification</l1>, or in one of the TEER category 2 or 3 occupations in sectors with labour shortages or tied to government priorities. These are the following sectors: natural and applied sciences, construction, health care, natural resources, education, sports and the military.
Mais attention, car le travailleur étran: But be careful, because the foreign worker must also hold a work permit with at least 16 months remaining at the time of the OWP application. It should also be added that the dependent children of foreign workers will no longer be eligible for an OWP.
Les PTO déjà délivrés et qui n’ont pas e: OWPs that have already been issued and have not expired remain valid. Family members of an international student who received a work permit shorter than the principal applicant’s permit can apply to renew their status. To do so, they must submit an application meeting the same criteria as their current work permit, for a duration equal to that of the study permit.
Une autre catégorie qui échappe à ces re: Another category exempt from these restrictions is the spouses or common-law partners of workers covered by free trade agreements and of those transitioning to permanent residence.
La seule option pour les personnes touch: The only option for people affected by this measure is to apply individually for a work permit, under the TFWP for example.
En fin de compte, l’intention du Canada: In the end, Canada’s intention is crystal clear: that all these measures, taken together, will bring down immigration numbers in 2025. Indeed, the targets for permanent residents (PRs) are now 395,000 instead of the 500,000 set for 2024. For 2026 and 2027, further decreases are planned to reach targets of 380,000, then 365,000 permanent residents.
En ce qui concerne les résidents non per: As for non-permanent residents, the federal government wants to bring their share of the population down from 6.5% to 5%. In 2025 and 2026, the target is 445,000 people a year, with an increase of 17,439 people in 2027.
Avec de telles mesures, les entreprises: With such measures, Quebec and Canadian businesses in certain sectors could become collateral victims of this change of course on immigration.
Les étudiants récemment diplômés au Québ: Students who recently graduated in Quebec can turn to the <l1>Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP)</l1>, a federal measure. Since November 1<sup>st</sup>, those holding a bachelor’s, master’s or doctoral degree or a diploma from a public college must pass an English or French language proficiency test.
Depuis le 1<sup>er</sup> janvier, le pro: Since January 1<sup>st</sup>, the program has been suspended. No new collective sponsorship applications are being processed. But this isn’t the first time the program has been suspended. The Liberal government halted it in 2017 because of processing backlogs, then again in 2020 amid suspicions of fraud. This time, Immigration Minister Jean-François Roberge says he made the decision to meet Quebec’s permanent immigration target for 2025, which involves cutting in half the number of refugees the province takes in.
